transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-05
Start time: 15:30 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Rina Okafor (Redwood CSM), Sarah Patel (Lynx - Head of Security), Daniel Moore (Lynx - Eng Manager), Priya Singh (Lynx - Cloud Architect), Evan Lee (Lynx - Procurement)

Summary (auto): security posture discovery; customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated; collecting compliance artifacts and integration steps.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time today. quick intro from our side, i'm maya, i'm the AE handling lynx.
[00:07] Sarah Patel: Hi, sarah here. thanks. we'll be looking at security posture and what we need to get approved for a pilot.
[00:12] Maya Chen: Great. diego, do you want to jump in on the technical side?
[00:15] Diego Alvarez: yeah, thanks. hi all. i'll go through our compliance posture, how we do identity, encryption, and what changes between hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
[00:25] Daniel Moore: quick context, we're a payment platform, must keep pii and payment metadata encrypted, retention is regulated. goal is to understand whether hosted api is acceptable or we need dedicated capacity or full private deployment.
[00:38] Priya Singh: also need to understand SAML SSO, our idp is okta, and our security team is strict on key management.
[00:45] Diego Alvarez: totally. starting with compliance - redwood has SOC 2 Type II and we're working toward ISO certs, we can share the SOC2 report and pen test summary. for hosted we provide logical tenant isolation and pgp style encryption, for dedicated you get reserved gpu pools and stronger tenancy guarantees.
[01:00] Sarah Patel: when you say "pgp style" are you talking customer-managed keys or keys managed by you? we need to see KMS options.
[01:07] Diego Alvarez: good question. for hosted we use provider-managed KMS by default, but we have a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) option for enterprise customers via AWS KMS or customer HSM in dedicated/private setups. there's a little nuance between BYOK and full external HSM — we can draw that out.
[01:22] Priya Singh: and how are keys rotated? we have requirements for regular rotation and for key material never leaving our control for certain datasets.
[01:30] Diego Alvarez: rotation is supported through the KMS provider—if you use BYOK you manage rotation on your side, and we integrate with your KMS using envelope encryption patterns so raw key material isn't stored in our infra. for private on-prem deployments you can run the KMS inside your network.
[01:45] Sarah Patel: ok. audit logging — what do you capture? we need immutable logs for access to data and admin actions for at least one year.
[01:52] Diego Alvarez: we emit audit logs for all control-plane and user API calls; logs include user identity, action, timestamp, and response codes. logs can be exported to customer S3 or pushed to SIEMs via syslog/agents. retention is configurable per customer on dedicated/private, hosted has default retention but we offer long-term retention add-on.
[02:10] Sarah Patel: default retention window?
[02:12] Diego Alvarez: hosted default is 90 days, add-on supports 1-7 years depending on retention tier. dedicated customers typically choose in-contract retention terms.
[02:20] Daniel Moore: are logs tamper-evident? chain of custody?
[02:23] Diego Alvarez: we provide integrity checks and can sign log bundles for customers on enterprise plans; for private deployments you control signage and storage.
[02:30] Evan Lee: vendor risk team will want copies of soc report and pen test, plus proof of encryption in transit at least.
[02:36] Maya Chen: we will share SOC 2 Type II and the latest pen test summary after the call.
[02:40] Sarah Patel: SSO — we use okta, and we need SAML metadata examples and instructions for scoping. does reddwood support SAML and SCIM?
[02:49] Diego Alvarez: yes, we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. we've got example metadata and sample IdP configs. note: sometimes transcription systems call it "sample" but it's saml 2.0.
[03:03] Priya Singh: any gotchas around roles and RBAC? we want fine-grained roles — audit, dev, admin, read-only, and ability to restrict model endpoints by team.
[03:12] Diego Alvarez: our RBAC model supports role-based policies and per-api-key scoping. you can bind roles to groups via SCIM. in dedicated/private you can opt for stronger network-level isolation and per-tenant VPC routing.
[03:24] Sarah Patel: how do you prevent data leakage between customers in hosted?
[03:28] Diego Alvarez: multi-tenant isolation at the application and storage layer; customer data is logically separated, models don't learn from customer prompts in hosted by default—there's a setting to opt-in to shared models but for enterprise we set it off.
[03:40] Daniel Moore: what about kv cache and prefix caching — could that leak?
[03:44] Diego Alvarez: the KV cache is per-model instance and per-tenant, not shared across tenants. i've seen the term "KV cash" in transcripts before, but it's KV cache.
[03:50] Sarah Patel: encryption at rest details? algorithms?
[03:53] Diego Alvarez: we use AES-256 for data at rest and TLS 1.2/1.3 for in-transit; keys backed by KMS providers. for high security customers we can integrate HSM-backed keys.
[04:03] Priya Singh: data residency — we need EU data to remain in eu, and some product telemetry in different regions. can you restrict region?
[04:10] Diego Alvarez: yes, we can route requests to region-specific clusters and store embeddings/indices in-region for dedicated/private. hosted customers can pick region endpoints; dedicated gives stronger guarantees and private is fully controlled.
[04:22] Sarah Patel: retention policy enforcement — we'd like the ability to auto-delete prompt logs after N days for regulated datasets.
[04:28] Diego Alvarez: we support configurable retention policies; for hosted there's a default and an opt-in auto-purge policy, for dedicated/private you define retention in the contract and we implement on storage layer.
[04:38] Evan Lee: procurement question — if we go dedicated, what's the minimum contract length and SLA?
[04:43] Maya Chen: typical dedicated is 12 months minimum for reserved capacity with SLA tiers; we can send a draft pricing sheet.
[04:49] Daniel Moore: technical detail request: do you support private networking / VPC peering and no public internet egress?
[04:55] Diego Alvarez: yes, VPC peering and private endpoints are supported for dedicated and private, and we can provide a private control plane option for private deployments. for hosted we do support VPC peering for enterprise customers with dedicated options.
[05:07] Sarah Patel: compliance questionnaires — will you fill out our security questionnaire? timeline?
[05:11] Maya Chen: we typically handle an initial security questionnaire, then hand off to the security team for deeper items. if you send the questionnaire we will triage and respond; larger enterprise questionnaires sometimes need 5-10 business days.
[05:22] Priya Singh: on model versioning — we need ability to pin model versions and rollback. any security concerns there?
[05:27] Diego Alvarez: model pinning is supported; from a security perspective we version runtime artifacts and maintain reproducible builds; we keep provenance logs for model uploads and rollouts.
[05:36] Sarah Patel: any certifications roadmap? you're SOC2 now, iso next?
[05:39] Maya Chen: yes SOC2 Type II in place, ISO 27001 in progress, we can share dates and roadmap in the follow up.
[05:46] Daniel Moore: what about penetration tests — do you allow us to run one against our dedicated instance?
[05:50] Diego Alvarez: for dedicated and private, yes — coordinated pen tests are allowed under an engagement plan. for hosted we'll share our internal pen test summaries but customer-initiated pen tests usually require tenancy-level separation or private deployment.
[05:58] Sarah Patel: ok makes sense.
[06:00] Maya Chen: wrapping up, action items and next steps. we'll send SOC2 and pen test summary, diego will put together a KMS/encryption diagram showing hosted vs dedicated, rina will schedule a 30-45 minute technical deep dive with priya and daniel next week.
[06:12] Priya Singh: i'll also send our SAML metadata and the IdP contact.
[06:16] Evan Lee: procurement will expect draft pricing and dedicated terms.
[06:19] Maya Chen: we'll include a draft dedicated pilot pricing and sample contract.
[06:22] Sarah Patel: thanks, this was helpful. one last clarification — do you have an option to purge embeddings immediately for certain datasets?
[06:29] Diego Alvarez: yes, we can do manual purge APIs and auto-purge policies, and for dedicated/private you can implement policy via lifecycle rules.
[06:36] Daniel Moore: cool. that should be enough to get internal approval to pilot.
[06:39] Maya Chen: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.

End of transcript.
